digest.overview:
The Trump administration sued in Alaska in a move that could block certification of the state's Senate race if the Republican incumbent loses, and President Trump exempted some Canadian imports from his 50% tariffs after Sen. Susan Collins raised their impact on Maine. Researchers say Kremlin-backed groups are stepping up influence efforts in the final stretch of the midterms, while the Justice Department plans to send more than twice as many election monitors as in 2022 on Nov. 3. Former FBI employees were charged with lying to Congress about the bureau's Hunter Biden inquiries. Wedgewood Polls admitted fabricating survey data that news outlets had cited. Severe flooding in the Four Corners region forced evacuations and rescues, with more rain expected this weekend. Treasury proposed a rule restricting U.S. investment in supercomputing and AI in China and other countries of concern. A CDC report put the U.S. birth rate at a record low.

Abroad, Israel's prime minister vowed a massive West Bank military operation after gunmen killed two soldiers at a checkpoint, and signs of fraying loyalty emerged in the Likud stronghold of Kiryat Shmona ahead of Tuesday's election. The White House said Melania Trump brokered a localized ceasefire in Ukraine's Oleshky. Venezuelans marched to demand democratic elections, and President Trump floated stopping U.S. warships in Cuba on their way home from the Middle East. In Yemen, drinking water is running short in Taiz as Houthi rebels tighten their siege. Officials are investigating whether the first Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria are linked. Residents tested years after the Lahaina wildfire showed high levels of toxic metals.

home.overview:
The Brewers drew first blood in the World Series, holding off the Rays 3–2 in Milwaukee as Trevor Megill struck out Jonny DeLuca with the bases loaded after a replay review wiped out a would-be game-ending double play. Christian Yelich, William Contreras and Jackson Chourio drove in the runs, and Game 2 is tonight. In the NBA, Jayson Tatum poured in 36 as Boston beat the Knicks 107–103, the Lakers took the Battle of LA 125–117 behind Austin Reaves, Amen Thompson's late block on Victor Wembanyama sealed Houston's 114–110 win in Austin, and Cooper Flagg was hurt on a flagrant foul in Dallas' rout at Indiana. In the NFL, Baker Mayfield returns for Tampa Bay, Lamar Jackson is questionable, and Sunday brings Steelers–Saints in Paris and Chiefs at Seattle.

Middlesbrough hammered Bolton 5–1 to go top of the Championship, Gladbach won 3–2 at Stuttgart and Ipswich drew 1–1 with Forest. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalized after collapsing at training. Man City visit Aston Villa today, Chelsea host Tottenham, Barcelona and Real Madrid meet in Sunday's El Clásico, and PSG–Lyon moves to Monday. FC Seoul clinched the K League 1 title with a 1–1 draw against Gangwon. In the KBO, Samsung's Chris Paddack faces Kia's James Naile in Sunday's second-round opener.

brief: The Brewers beat the Rays 3–2 in World Series Game 1 in Milwaukee to take a 1–0 series lead.
Christian Yelich tripled in a first-inning run, William Contreras drove in another, and Jackson Chourio added a seventh-inning RBI single.
Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run over five innings, and the Brewers' bullpen struck out six over the final four.
Trevor Megill escaped a bases-loaded ninth, striking out Jonny DeLuca after a review overturned a would-be game-ending double play.
Jonathan Aranda went 3-for-3 for Tampa Bay in the loss.
Game 2 is tonight at 8 p.m. ET in Milwaukee, with Drew Rasmussen listed for the Rays against Logan Henderson.
